newsitem.title: USA: U.S. targets four nations for trade reviews.
newsitem.headline: U.S. targets four nations for trade reviews.

text.p: The United States announced Tuesday it was challenging Indonesia, Brazil and Australia over trade policies that affect the U.S. automobile industry and Argentina for high import tariffs on textiles and shoes.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Indonesia, Australia and Argentina will be challenged in the World Trade Organization.
Brazil will face an investigation under the so-called Section 301 U.S. trade law which allows retaliation against unfair trade practices.
Motor vehicle manufacturing accounts for one out of every 10 U.S. jobs in durable goods manufacturing, and the United States is one of the world's largest automobile manufacturers.

Barshefsky said the U.S. was challenging domestic content rules in Indonesia, tariff laws in Brazil that favor domestically-produced parts, Australian subsidies that encourage export of leather for automobile upholstery, and 35 percent import duties in Argentina for textiles, apparel and footwear.
Barshefsky also announced that Germany had agreed to take steps that would ensure open competition in its heavy electrical equipment market.
The changes will assure equitable treatment of U.S. firms, she said, but the United States will not withdraw potential trade action against Germany until the reforms were put into law.
